question: New goods traffic bans introduced by the Tyrol Region in January 2024

In its response to written question E-000348/20201, the Commission discussed whether the decision published in Tyrol Official Journal No 81/2019 amending Section 3(1) of sector-specific traffic ban No 44/2016 was incompatible with EU law, particularly in the light of Court of Justice case-law.

As justification, the Commission cited the Court’s ruling that the measures in force at the time excluding lorries with a laden mass exceeding 7.5 tonnes from a section of the A12 motorway infringed Articles 34 and 35 TFEU.

On 1 January 2021, the government of the Federal State of Tyrol supplemented the aforementioned traffic bans on the A12 motorway by unilaterally introducing a further series of restrictions on heavy goods traffic through the Brenner pass. On 13 January 2024, the State of Tyrol introduced new measures excluding vehicles with a laden mass exceeding 7.5 tonnes from the A12 and A13 motorways between the hours of 7.
00 and 15.00. In the light of the above: 1.
Has the Commission finished its evaluation of Decision No 81/2019?
Can the Commission confirm that both the above decision and the additional restrictions imposed by the State of Tyrol are indeed incompatible with EU law?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (12.3.2024) The Commission together with the Member States concerned has explored ways forward to solve the issues relating to the traffic situation through the Brenner pass and it still encourages the Member States concerned to agree on a common package of measures. The Commission continues to closely monitor the situation and reserves the possibility of taking any appropriate measures in accordance with the powers conferred to it by the Treaties.
